title: U.S. News Analysis: ICE Custody Deaths at 26 in 2026, On Pace to Shatter Record
excerpt: A U.S. News & World Report analysis drawing on data from multiple watchdog organizations found that with 26 deaths reported through the first seven months of 2026, the ICE custody death toll is on pace to exceed 2025's record by more than 25%, with researchers linking the surge to detention expansion and medical care failures.
content:
On August 13, 2026, U.S. News & World Report published a data-driven analysis tracking ICE detainee deaths, compiling figures from the UCLA Behind Bars Data Project, ICE official reports, and several advocacy organizations.

  • With 26 deaths reported through the first seven months of 2026, the pace is on track to exceed 2025's total by more than 25%.
  • The 31 deaths in ICE custody in calendar year 2025 eclipsed the total number of deaths in the four prior years combined.
  • An investigation of Delaney Hall documented contaminated food, extreme temperatures, overcrowding, and a detainee with active tuberculosis.
  • The count does not include individuals killed during ICE enforcement actions or post-release deaths where dates cannot be established — meaning the true toll is likely higher than official figures.

The NIPNLG separately reported as of September 1, 2026, that at least 26 people had died in ICE custody in 2026, noting the pace made it likely that 2026 would break 2025's record death toll. Advocacy groups pointed to the June 2026 ICE policy eliminating post-release death reporting as a factor suppressing official counts.
